we have developed POPE, an ontology for pharmaceutical drug development, that models phases, material properties and structures, experiments, and unit operations and that we have used the ontology to develop a software tool that can be used for knowledge management and knowledge generation.
we developed POPE, a comprehensive ontology for pharmaceutical engineering that is publicly available, to model the information and knowledge in pharmaceutical drug development and manufacture.

the development of a knowledge base that is capable of representing information and knowledge in the pharmaceutical industry.
development of POPE as a common, explicit, platform-independent vocabulary for pharmaceutical engineering.
developing an ontology that will be used to facilitate information exchange, knowledge discovery, and knowledge management.

the POPE framework is a powerful tool that can be used to facilitate the development and use of ontologies in pharmaceutical drug development and production.

the POPE ontology is a powerful and useful tool to facilitate the development, implementation, and use of a knowledge-based pharmaceutical engineering system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a conceptual framework for POPE, which has the potential to be a common, explicit, platform-independent vocabulary for pharmaceutical engineering.
we have developed a conceptual framework and a platform-independent, open-source, extensible, and scalable ontology to support pharmaceutical engineering and related areas.
we developed an ontology that is both a knowledge representation tool and a platform for data integration and exchange.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a common, explicit, platform-independent vocabulary is needed to streamline knowledge and information generation and management.
the use of an explicit vocabulary in pharmaceutical informatics is essential for the development and use of interoperable software tools.
